stories.title: Nvidia board reportedly weighs ousting Jensen Huang amid affair claims
stories.summary: Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang after a second alleged affair surfaced, days after he admitted to one with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy; Nvidia's stock dropped and Congress has called him in to explain.
stories.more: The New York Times reported that Nvidia's board is preparing to dismiss Huang following a second alleged affair, this time with an Nvidia executive, just days after he admitted to a separate relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. The news sent Nvidia's stock down as the board could reportedly act as soon as Wednesday evening, ending Huang's 33-year run as founder and CEO. House Republicans have called on Huang to answer in a closed-door briefing about the alleged spy affair, and lawmakers are pressing for a hearing. With Nvidia having no public succession plan, TechCrunch published a list of potential replacements, from internal executives to outside candidates, underscoring how unprepared the company appears for a leadership change.

stories.title: Meta's longtime head of infrastructure Santosh Janardhan steps down
stories.summary: Santosh Janardhan, who joined Meta in 2009 and has long led its infrastructure organization, is stepping down from the role, TechCrunch reports.
stories.more: Janardhan has overseen Meta's infrastructure for years as the company has ramped up AI-related data center and compute spending. TechCrunch did not report who will succeed him or when the departure takes effect.

stories.title: CoreWeave leans on prepayments and shorter deals to fund AI growth
stories.summary: CoreWeave is increasingly asking customers to pay upfront, borrowing against specific contracts, and weighing shorter-term deals that could mean higher prices, according to its third-quarter earnings, TechCrunch reports.
stories.more: The shift suggests CoreWeave is managing cash flow pressures as it continues to build out GPU capacity for AI customers. TechCrunch notes that leaning on shorter contracts and prepayments could eventually push prices higher for customers.

stories.title: US corporate AI spending growth slows to 1.65% in October
stories.summary: US corporate AI spending hit a new high in October but growth slowed to just 1.65%, according to the Ramp AI Index, with one percent of companies still driving 80% of OpenAI and Anthropic's revenue.
stories.more: Customer support is emerging as a new growth driver for enterprise AI spending, the index found, though it may carry lower margins than the coding use cases that have driven spending so far. The concentration of revenue among a small share of companies suggests AI adoption, while broad, remains shallow relative to a handful of heavy users.

stories.title: TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic and OpenAI
stories.summary: Taiwan's chipmaking giant TSMC plans to invest $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI, the latest example of the AI boom's circular financing between chipmakers and model developers, Ars Technica reports.
stories.more: The investment follows a pattern of chipmakers and cloud providers taking stakes in the AI labs that buy their hardware, deepening financial ties across the AI supply chain. Ars Technica frames the deal as the latest sign of the AI trade's 'circular financing,' arriving as broader AI-related markets wobble.

stories.title: AWS ships local service emulator built by a swarm of AI agents
stories.summary: AWS released an official emulator for running tests against local clones of its many services without needing a paid API key. Written in Rust, the project was built by a large swarm of AI agents, racking up 29,684 commits in its first three weeks.
stories.more: Simon Willison noted the emulator currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows, and hopes that limitation is addressed in the future. AWS's Swami Sivasubramanian wrote about the project's origin in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog. The scale of AI-written code -- nearly 30,000 commits in three weeks -- highlights how far agentic coding has advanced for infrastructure tooling. Hacker News discussion also raised the broader question of what engineers' jobs look like when agents write the code.

stories.title: LLM CLI tool patches API key leak bug in custom endpoint config
stories.summary: The llm command-line tool shipped version 0.37.2, fixing a security issue reported by Daniel de Araujo that could leak a configured OpenAI API key to other OpenAI-compatible providers.
stories.more: The bug affected extra-openai-models.yaml, the mechanism llm uses to connect to OpenAI-compatible endpoints from other providers, now managed via the new 'llm openai endpoint add' command added in version 0.37. The key could leak under two conditions: when the named api_key_name had never been stored, or in certain cases involving the 'responses' configuration. Two GitHub Security Advisories, GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w, document the issue.

stories.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code verifies Signal's crypto core in weeks
stories.summary: Google DeepMind says its AlphaProof Code system mathematically verified Signal's cryptographic core in four weeks, a process that typically takes years, using Gemini Carbon-powered agents that wrote over six million lines of proof code.
stories.more: The agents flagged only about one percent of the generated proof code for human review, according to DeepMind. The company says it plans to extend the verification method to other critical infrastructure, including power grids and medical devices. The achievement points to formal verification as an emerging use case for AI coding agents beyond writing application code.

stories.title: New benchmark tests generalist AI models across tabular data tasks
stories.summary: Researchers introduced the One Table Benchmark, spanning 56 datasets, 46 methods, and 20 capability axes, to test whether a single AI model can handle tabular data generation, imputation, and prediction equally well.
stories.more: The benchmark evaluates five backbone models to see whether these three distinct query types -- which probe different aspects of the same tabular data distribution -- share capabilities or require separate specialized training. Prior evaluations typically tested generation, imputation, and prediction in isolation, leaving it unclear how their training objectives interact. The paper compares task rankings on aligned data splits and explicit task contracts across all 56 datasets. It remains unclear from the paper whether any single model family consistently outperforms across all three task types.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini Decisions API with new Gemini Decision 1 model
stories.summary: Google DeepMind launched the Gemini Decisions API, powered by a new Gemini Decision 1 model that scores up to 1,000 closed-ended questions per call across text, image, audio, and video in 150-250ms, undercutting OpenAI's and Jev's pricing.
stories.more: Gemini Decision 1 can score up to 1,000 closed-ended questions in a single pass across text, images, audio, and video, returning results in 150 to 250 milliseconds at roughly five times lower cost than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, according to Google. Simon Willison noted the API is nearly identical to Jev, supporting the same three question types -- yes/no, multiple choice, and rubric scoring -- and even reusing Jev's term 'Noul' for a yes/no question. Pricing matches OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna decision model at 10 cents per million input tokens with free output, while Jev remains the cheapest of the three at 4.2 cents per million tokens, though Jev is text and JSON only. The move makes Google the third major lab to enter the decision-model category this year.

stories.title: Startup Radical Numerics builds AI model to detect AI-engineered pathogens
stories.summary: Radical Numerics has built a model that it says can identify both natural and AI-engineered pathogens without needing an internet connection, aiming to counter the risk of AI-assisted bioweapons, Wired reports.
stories.more: The startup's offline-capable approach is designed to let biosecurity screening happen even where internet access is unavailable or untrusted. Wired did not detail how the model was trained or validated, leaving open how well it performs against novel threats.

items.title: A Startup Wants to Fight AI Bioweapons With AI

stories.title: United Airlines bars AI agents from booking flights for travelers
stories.summary: United says it won't let personal AI assistants book tickets on its flights, citing privacy and regulatory concerns, even though few customers have tried it so far.
stories.more: United says it won't let personal AI assistants book tickets on its flights, citing both privacy and regulatory concerns about autonomous agents acting on a customer's behalf. The airline told The Wall Street Journal it hasn't yet seen many travelers try to use AI agents for bookings, a pattern other businesses such as DoorDash have also observed. The policy makes United one of the first major carriers to publicly set rules around AI agent use at the point of purchase.

stories.summary: After the indie game Big Walk used AI to fix a bug, Independent Games Festival judges and the indie gaming community began reassessing how much AI use in development is acceptable, Ars Technica reports.
stories.more: Ars Technica reports that for many Independent Games Festival judges, any amount of AI-assisted coding is considered disqualifying. The incident has reignited debate within the indie development community over where to draw the line on AI tool use.

stories.title: Data center boom runs into permitting, power, and opposition delays
stories.summary: TechCrunch reports the AI data center boom is colliding with local opposition, permitting delays, and electricity shortages, raising doubts that many announced projects will actually get built despite billions in planned AI infrastructure spending.
stories.more: The challenges start before construction even begins, as many announced data center projects may never break ground given the scale of obstacles developers face. TechCrunch's reporting, covered in both video and podcast formats, ties the slowdown to a wave of local pushback against new builds. Billions of dollars in AI infrastructure commitments are at stake as companies race to secure the power needed to run them.
